title: Federally paid meals in child care: sponsors, sites and what a day can hold
question: Do the meal numbers fit inside the federal limit of three eating occasions a day, and is every meal site a licensed child-care site?
finding: The State publishes meals, children fed and enrolment only as county totals, so no sponsor can be tested. At that level the numbers fit: in 2024-25 centres and after-school sites claimed 3,547,122 meals for 11,147 people fed on an average day, 1.22 per person per weekday, and family child-care homes 2.54, against a federal ceiling of three; no year exceeds three, and the average paid per meal never exceeds the top federal rate. Enrolment is the number that does not behave: 23,993 in 2018-19 to 126,299 in 2019-20 while sites went from 243 to 251 and children fed on an average day from 12,104 to 9,750; 19,697 in 2020-21 to 65,919 in 2021-22 while sites went from 303 to 311 and children fed on an average day from 13,743 to 15,091. Of 119 meal sites of a child-care type, 7 have no centre licence at the listed address (7 of them school-district sites). The State's count of family-home meal sites reads 5,405 in 2022-23 against 351 in 2024-25, which looks like an error in the source.
how: The federal rule (title 7, section 226.17) says: "Reimbursement must not be claimed for more than two meals and one snack or one meal and two snacks provided daily to each child." Meals per person per weekday is the county's meals claimed, divided by average daily participation, divided by the weekdays in that federal fiscal year; three a day on every weekday is the ceiling drawn on the chart. Average paid per meal is reimbursement divided by meals, set against the highest federal rate for a free lunch or supper in the two rate years that overlap. Sponsor rows come from the State's current list of participating centres: each site was matched to a centre licence by licence number or address, then by name and ZIP code. Summer-meal rows count sites on the federal site finder; 20 of the 55 sites listed for summer 2026 are at an address with a child-care centre licence.
limits: Meal counts, attendance and enrolment by sponsor and by site are not published; the State releases them only on a data request, and that record is what would allow a real test. A county average under three a day cannot rule out a single site over the limit. The federal rule exempts emergency shelters from licensing and lets after-school sites take part where no licence is required, and a preschool on a school campus may be licensed under a different street address, so a site with no licence at its address is a reason to check the address, not a finding. The notes kept with these reports warn that enrolment is not a head count of distinct people; the reports do not explain the jumps.
